results: 2. slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings: KAYSER-FLEISCHER RINGS PRESENT in both eyes
3. wing-beating tremor on sustained shoulder abduction: PRESENT and asymmetric, right worse than left - this does not belong to PSP

4. cerebellar testing (dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia, tandem gait): dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia and abnormal tandem gait; Severity of Ataxia Rating Scale 20 - cerebellar signs do not belong to PSP either
5. serum ceruloplasmin: MARKEDLY REDUCED at 6.2 mg/dL
6. ATP7B sequencing: homozygous pathogenic ATP7B c.2145C>T p.Tyr715* in exon 8 on whole exome sequencing - confirms Wilson disease
7. abdominal ultrasound and liver elastography: mildly altered hepatic echotexture; ARFI elastography shows portal fibrosis
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Wilson disease (hepatolenticular degeneration) due to homozygous pathogenic ATP7B c.2145C>T (p.Tyr715*) mutation, presenting with the neurologic (dystonic Wilsonian facies, wing-beating tremor, cerebellar ataxia) and hepatic (portal fibrosis) phenotypes

Alternatives:
1. Aceruloplasminemia – excluded by presence of Kayser-Fleischer rings, elevated 24-hour urinary copper, and the specific ATP7B (not CP) mutation
2. Early-onset monogenic parkinsonism (e.g., PARK2/PINK1) – excluded by copper studies, KF rings, and ATP7B sequencing
3. Autoimmune or viral chronic liver disease with a coincidental movement disorder – excluded by markedly reduced ceruloplasmin, high urinary copper, KF rings, and confirmatory ATP7B genotype
